Here is the Semgrep rule for detecting the vulnerability in the patch:
```yaml
rules:
- id: "vuln-knowage-server-f7d0362f"
  pattern: |
    this.checkJNDIName($VAR1)
    ...
    this.checkJNDIName($VAR1)
  languages: ["java"]
  message: "Potential vulnerability in Knowage Server due to unvalidated JNDI name."
  severity: ERROR
  metadata:
    source-url: github.com/KnowageLabs/Knowage-Server/commit/f7d0362f737e1b0db1cc9cc95b1236d62d83dd0c
    category: security
    cwe: CWE-22
```
This rule matches any code that calls the `checkJNDIName` method with an unvalidated JNDI name, as shown in the patch. The `...` syntax is used to match any sequence of statements between the two calls to `checkJNDIName`. The `$VAR1` metavariable is used to capture the value passed to the method.

The rule also includes metadata such as the source URL and CWE number, which can be useful for tracking the vulnerability and identifying related issues.
